correctness.rationale: From the normalized two-index Gnedin--Olshanski marginal, both q-binomial substitutions are justified in q<|z|<1/q by geometric absolute domination. The resulting characteristic product equals the bilateral pgf of the difference of two a.s.-finite iid sums of independent geometric variables; equality of Laurent coefficients gives equality in distribution. Its value at z=-1 is a product of strictly positive factors with absolutely summable logarithms; termwise logarithmic differentiation on compact parameter intervals yields a strictly negative series, proving both monotonicities. A stand-alone standard-library exact-source-series versus product diagnostic passes 30 numerical assertions with explicit truncation bounds. This is an analytic infinite proof, not an extrapolation from tests.
residual_risks: The diagnostic uses finite-precision Decimal arithmetic; infinite assertions rely entirely on the displayed analytic proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a new natural representation of a stationary permutation displacement as the difference of iid sums of independent geometric variables, together with its full bilateral pgf. It establishes the exact previously conjectured sign c_o(Q)>1/2>c_e(Q) and proves both strict parameter-monotonicities for all Q>1, simultaneously resolving two explicit 2022 open problems rather than an arbitrary normalization exercise. It also reproduces both parameter-boundary limits and isolates the useful exact parity gap.
